question_text: Calculate the conductivity at $200^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ of (a) copper (annealed standard) and (b) tungsten. Give your answer as a tuple: (copper_conductivity, tungsten_conductivity).The units of each required answer are (Ω^-1·m^-1, Ω^-1·m^-1), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

For metals, resistivity varies approximately linearly with temperature:

$$\rho(T) = \rho_{20}\bigl[1 + \alpha\,(T - 20)\bigr]$$

Since conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity, $\sigma = 1/\rho$:

$$\sigma(T) = \frac{\sigma_{20}}{1 + \alpha\,(T - 20)}$$

Using standard room-temperature (20 °C) values (Callister):

| Metal | $\sigma_{20}$ (Ω⁻¹·m⁻¹) | $\alpha$ (°C⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|
| Copper (annealed) | $6.0\times10^{7}$ | $0.0039$ |
| Tungsten | $1.8\times10^{7}$ | $0.0045$ |

With $T = 200\,°\text{C}$, so $\Delta T = 180\,°\text{C}$:

**(a) Copper**
$$\sigma_{\text{Cu}} = \frac{6.0\times10^{7}}{1 + 0.0039(180)} = \frac{6.0\times10^{7}}{1.702} \approx 3.53\times10^{7}\;\Omega^{-1}\text{·m}^{-1}$$

**(b) Tungsten**
$$\sigma_{\text{W}} = \frac{1.8\times10^{7}}{1 + 0.0045(180)} = \frac{1.8\times10^{7}}{1.81} \approx 9.94\times10^{6}\;\Omega^{-1}\text{·m}^{-1}$$

$$\boxed{(3.53\times10^{7},\; 9.94\times10^{6})}$$
